question.text: In an IPO, what percentage of the anchor investor portion is reserved for domestic mutual funds?

explanation.text: The Logic: Of the anchor investor portion, 40% is reserved, with one-third (33%) earmarked for domestic mutual funds and 7% for life insurance companies and pension funds. The Trap: 50% is tempting because candidates may assume an equal split. The actual split within the 40% reserved portion is 33:7 (mutual funds vs insurance/pension). Note: The 33% earmark for domestic mutual funds and the 7% earmark for insurance/pension together make up the 40% reserved portion of the anchor allocation.
